__
 
• **A series of hydrocarbons** having **similar chemical properties** and **sharing the same general formula** constitute a **homologous series**. 
 
• Each member of a homologous series differs from the succeeding or preceding member by CH2.
 
• These organic compounds** have a similar structure and functional group**.
 
• The hydrocarbons in a homologous series **show a gradation in physical properties**.
 
• For example- CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈,... represent the homologous series of **alkanes** having general formula as **CₙH****₂ₙ₊₂****, **where n denotes the number of carbon atoms**. **Successive terms of the series differ by CH₂.
 
• Similarly, C₂H4, C3H6, C4H8,... represent the homologous series of **alkenes** having general formula as **CnH****2n**. Here also, the successive terms differ by CH2.
 
• Also, C₂H₂, C₃H₄, C₄H₆,... represent the homologous series of **alkynes **having general formula as **CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. **Again the successive terms differ by CH2.
 
• Clearly, **C2H6 and C3H9 are not part of the homologous series as they do not differ by the molecular formula of CH****2** but differ by CH3.​

• **​**All members of a homologous series can be **represented by a** **general formula**.
 
• Each member of a homologous series **differs** **from its successive or preceding member** **by the molecular formula of CH****2**.
 
• Each member of a homologous series **differs from its successive or preceding member by the molecular mass of 14**.
 
• All members of a homologous series can be** prepared by the same general method**.
 
• All members of a homologous series have the** same chemical properties** due to the presence of the same functional group.
 
• Due to different molecular masses, members of a homologous series **show differences in physical properties** like melting point, boiling point, solubility, etc.** but with a gradation**.

questions.question: In 1942, who presented the "Trophic-dynamic aspect of Ecology," which is the basic process of energy transfer from one trophic level to another in an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Raymond L Lindeman**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Trophic-dynamic aspect of ecology:**

__
 
• The fundamental process by which energy moves from one trophic level to the next in an ecosystem is known as trophic dynamics.

**Energy flow in the ecosystem:**

 
• In a food chain, the energy flow follows the 10 per cent law.
 
• According to this law, only **10 per cent of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the other; the rest is lost into the atmosphere.**
 
• This energy is stored in various organic products in the plants from the sun via the process of photosynthesis.
 
• This is then** passed on to the primary consumers in the food chain when the herbivores consume (primary consumers) the plants as food.**
 
• Then conversion of chemical energy stored in plant products into kinetic energy occurs, degradation of energy will occur through its conversion into heat.
 
• **The energy flow is: Primary (100%) → First level/ Primary (10%) → Second-level/ Secondary (1%) → Third level / Tertiary (0.1%).**
 
• **The energy flow in the ecosystem is clearly unidirectional**.
 
• The** ten percent rule of transfer of energy** from one trophic level to the next is being credited to **Raymond Lindeman (1942).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Arthur Tansley:**

 
• It was in **1935 that Arthur Tansley**, the British ecologist, **coined the term 'ecosystem'**.
 
• It is the **interactive system established between the biocoenosis (the group of living creatures), and their biotope**, the environment in which they live.

**Ernst Haeckel:**

 
• The word **“Ecology” was coined by “Ernst Haeckel”**.
 
• It is the branch of biology that studies organizations in their environment.
 
• Ecology word is taken from the** Greek word Oekologie, Oikos meaning “House” and logos meaning “Study”**.
 
• **Ecology is the study of the household**.
 
• Ernst Haeckel** also proposed the theory of development and evolution**.

**Charles Elton:**

 
• The **concept of the ecological pyramid was first proposed by Charles Elton in 1927.**
 
• It was known as the **Eltonian pyramid** then.** E.P. Odum wrote the popular ecology book 'Fundamentals of Ecology' in 1953**.

• The book **"Muntakhab-al-Tawarikh"** was written by **Abd al-Qadir Badauni.**

 
 
• He began writing this history in the first half of **1590**.
 
• The book was completed in **October 1595**.
 
• It comprises the **618 solar year's** historic events.
 
• This book is based on Khawaja Nizam-ud-din Ahmad Sirhindi's Tabaqat-i-Akbar Shahi.
 
 
 
• This work in three volumes is a general history of the Muslims of India:
 
 
• The first contains the rulers and kings of **Ghaznavids, Ghurid dynasty, Mamluk Dynasty, Babur, and Humayun**.
 
• Second, covers the first 40 years of Mughal Emperor Akbar's reign from **14 February 1556 to October 1595.**
 
• The third contains biographical accounts of the Saints, Poets who were attached to the court of Akbar.
 
 
 
• The accounts relate to **38 Shaykhs, 69 scholars, 15 philosophers, physicians, and 67 poets**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Akbar (1556-1605)**

• He was the son of **Humayun and Hamida Banu Begum, born at Amarkot in c. 1542 CE.**
 
• He was crowned at Kalanaur in c. 1556 CE at the young age of 13 years and 4 months.
 
• Akbar's biography is **Akabarnama** written by **Abul Fazal**.
 
• The Akbar Nama is divided into **three** books: The first book dealt with **Akbar's ancestors**. The second recorded the events of **Akbar's reign**. The third is the **Ain-i Akbari**.

**Dara Shikoh (1615-1659)**

• He is known as a pioneer of the academic movement for interfaith understanding in India. He had a deep understanding and knowledge of major religions, particularly Islam and Hinduism.
 
• He was assassinated by Aurangzeb, in a bitter struggle for the throne on 30th August 1659 when he was 44.
 
• He translated the Upanishads and other important sources of Hindu religion and spirituality from Sanskrit to Persian. Through these translations, he was responsible for taking the Hindu culture and spiritual traditions to Europe and the West.

**Jahanara Begum Sahib (1614-1681)**

 
• She was the eldest daughter of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• Together with her brother Dara Shikoh, she was a disciple of Mullah Shah Badakhshi, who initiated her into the Qadiriyya Sufi order in 1641.
 
• Jahanara Begum made such progress on the Sufi path that Mullah Shah would have named her his successor in the Qadiriyya, but the rules of the order did not allow this.
 
• She wrote a biography of **Moinuddin Chishti**, the founder of the Chishtiyah order, titled "**Mu'nis al-Arwāḥ"**, as well as a biography of Mullah Shah, titled **Risalah-i Şāḥibiyah,** in which she also described her initiation by him.

__
 
• Ulothrix is a genus of green algae in the family **Ulotrichaceae.**
 
• Ulothrix is a genus of **non-branching filamentous green algae,** generally **found in fresh and marine water.**
 
• The cells are **normally as broad as they are long**, and they thrive in the **low temperatures of spring and winter.**
 
• **Ulothix has one chloroplast present which is girdle shaped.**
 
• **Pyrenoids** are remain attached to the chloroplasts and are 1 to 4 in number.
 
• **Reproduction in Ulothrix** takes place by **means of vegetative, asexual, and sexual methods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Algae:**

__
 
• Algae are **chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both fresh water and marine) organisms.**
 
• **They occur in a variety of other habitats:** 
 
 
• **Moist stones, soils and wood.**
 
 
 
• Some of them also occur in **association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear).**
 
• The form and size of algae is **highly variable**, ranging from **colonial forms like Volvox and the filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra.**
 
• A few of the marine forms such as **kelps, form massive plant bodies.**
 
• The algae **reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods.**

**Vegetative Reproduction:**

 
• It occurs by fragmentation, tubers, stolons, adventitious branches, etc. Each fragment gets developed into an independent thalloid plant body.

**Asexual Reproduction:**

 
• **​**It occurs by a number of accessory spores, such as zoospores, aplanospores, carpospores, etc. The most common are the zoospores, which are flagellated.

**Sexual reproduction: **

 
• It takes place through** fusion of two gametes. **
 
• On the basis of the morphology of reproductive cells, Sexual Reproduction is of** three types:**

Isogamous:

 
• ​These **gametes** can be** flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix)** or **non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra).**

Anisogamous:

 
• Fusion of two gametes** dissimilar in size**, as in species of **Eudorina.**

Oogamous:

 
• Fusion between **one large**, **nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete **is termed** **like** Volvox, Fucus.**

• The error here lies in the Subject-Verb agreement.
 
• **Subject-verb agreement** is a grammatical rule that states that the subject of a sentence must agree in number with the verb.
 
• If the subject is singular, the verb must be singular, and if the subject is plural, the verb must be plural.
 
• In the given sentence "**the mother**" is a singular subject, the verb should be "**was**" instead of "**were**."
 
• The phrase "**as well as**" doesn't affect the subject-verb agreement; it is an additional element providing information about the subjects but doesn't change the singular nature of "the mother."

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence:** *The mother as well as the sons was asked to appear before the magistrate for interrogation. *
